title: routing-policy-decomposition-and-adapter-matrix
content:
Purpose
This is a working decomposition for the control-plane surface (API gateway, orchestration, runtime adapters) focused on routing policy responsibilities and multi-region decision points. Goal is to produce a clear ownership map and a minimal routing matrix we can use for design, testing, and runbooks.

Context & motivation
- Recent incidents where incorrect routing logic caused cross-region burst traffic and increased cost (see PLAT-1243).
- We need explicit boundaries so teams can iterate independently: e.g., API gateway can enforce tenancy/rate limits without having to understand runtime-level batching.
- Platform must support: latency-sensitive (interactive chat), throughput-oriented (batch embeddings), and regulated workloads (data residency + private deployments).

High-level goals
- Clear ownership for each control-plane responsibility.
- Simple, testable routing policy primitives (latency, cost, capacity, affinity, residency).
- Runtime adapters expose capability signals (max-seq, quantized-support, burst-concurrency) used by orchestrator for decisions.
- Minimize cross-service synchronous calls during request path to reduce p99.

Assumptions / constraints
- Customers can pin model versions and require model-level rollouts (canary).
- Some customers are on Dedicated pools (reserved capacity) and must be routed there by policy.
- Regions may have different model availability / hardware (e.g., A100 in us-west, H100 in eu-central).
- Control plane control messages (rollouts, configs) can be eventually consistent; however, routing decisions for live requests must use a consistent snapshot cached at edge for at least 30s.

Routing primitives (simple building blocks)
- region_affinity: prefer same-region runtime when latency delta < threshold.
- cost_tier: prefer lower-cost model variant when latency penalty < tolerance.
- capacity_respect: avoid routing to runtime pools reported as < 20% free capacity.
- tenant_isolation: route tenant->dedicated pools when tenant.has_dedicated == true.
- canary_split: split percent for rollout percentages at request-level.
- data_residency_required: enforce routing only to regions/pools with residency tag.

Proposed responsibility map (component -> responsibilities)
- API Gateway (eng: platform-api):
  - Ingress, authentication, per-tenant rate quotas, basic request validation.
  - Attach request metadata (tenant id, sticky-region hint if present, client SLA tier).
  - Short-circuit decisions for tenant_isolation and data_residency_required where straightforward.
  - Forward to Orchestrator proxy with enriched context; NOT to run complex multi-hop routing.

- Orchestrator/Control Plane (eng: control-plane):
  - Central policy decision engine: evaluate routing primitives against current state and return a target runtime endpoint or adapter.
  - Maintain model catalog, rollout configs, policy rules, and regional capability index.
  - Subscribe to runtime adapters health/capacity signals and provide aggregated view.
  - Responsible for canary_rollouts, fallback policies, automatic variant downgrade on quality regression triggers.
  - Expose a read-optimized cache (edge-cache) that API gateway can call for low-latency mapping.

- Runtime Adapters / Pool Managers (eng: serving-runtime):
  - Publish capability descriptors (max_seq_len, supported_quant, qmemory_estimate, credit_headroom) via heartbeat.
  - Accept runtime-specific routing (e.g., shard->model-variant mapping) and perform token-level batching and KV cache management.
  - Enforce local admission control (reject when overcommit) and return precise capacity hints.
  - Offer telemetry hooks for tracing and cost accounting (per-token counters).

- Router Proxy (lightweight edge component) (eng: infra-networking):
  - Local cached snapshot of orchestrator mapping to reduce synchronous calls.
  - Fast failover to alternate runtime within same region when adapter signals rapid degradation.
  - Collect per-route metrics and small buffer for speculative re-routing.

Routing decision flow (happy path)
1) Client -> API Gateway (auth, quota, enrich metadata)
2) Gateway calls Router Proxy cache for decision (if hit and fresh -> return target) else call Central Orchestrator API.
3) Orchestrator evaluates policy primitives (tenant_isolation, region_affinity, cost_tier, capacity_respect) and returns best candidate runtime adapter endpoint + fallback list.
4) Gateway forwards request (or streams) directly to runtime adapter endpoint. Runtime adapter enforces local admission control and proceeds.

Notes on multi-region consistency
- Coordinator model: single logical control-plane with regionally replicated read stores. Writes (policy changes) are applied through a sequenced pipeline; we accept eventual consistency for new routing configs but require monotonic snapshot versions so edges can detect stale configs.
- Snapshot versioning: every decision cache item includes a version + TTL; Router Proxy rejects items older than min_version_hint (sent by orchestrator when a migration/rollout occurs).
- Cross-region failover: default: prefer same-region; if latency exceeded or capacity low, failover to nearest-region respecting data-residency flags.

Ownership matrix (quick reference)
- API Gateway: platform-api team. Responsible: ingress auth, quotas, metadata enrichment, edge caching hooks.
- Orchestrator API: control-plane team. Responsible: policy engine, rollouts, model catalog, mapping decisions.
- Router Proxy: infra-networking. Responsible: low-latency cache + fast failover.
- Runtime Adapters: serving-runtime team. Responsible: capabilities, admission, batching, telemetry.
- Console / Rollouts UI: product-console. Responsible: exposing policies as editable configs and audit logs.

Operational playbooks (short)
- Incident: high cross-region traffic spike
  - Pager -> infra-networking + control-plane
  - Immediate action: control-plane push emergency policy to prefer dedicated-pools and tighten cost_tier; Router Proxy invalidate cache.
  - If unknown cause: scale up telemetry sampling.

Open questions / TODOs
- How to express complex quality-based routing (e.g., prefer variant A for prompts with certain safety footprint)? Proposed: augment Orchestrator with prompt-class classifier; needs privacy review.
- Should Gateway enforce tenant_isolation fully (quick reject) or just short-circuit to orchestrator? Current leaning: quick reject for dedicated tenants to reduce unnecessary orchestrator load.
- Admission control contract between Orchestrator and Runtime Adapter: need small JSON schema for capacity hints (fields: free_slots_estimate, token_budget, last_heartbeat_ms). Create PLAT task to spec.
- Performance target: end-to-end decision latency (Gateway->RouterProxy->Orchestrator) should be < 8ms on cache-hit path; measurable in synthetic tests.

Next steps
- Action item: Marisol/GitHub PR to add capacity_hint schema (due 2024-10-01).
- Action item: Daniel to prototype Router Proxy cached snapshot + invalidation API (PLAT-1243 follow-up).
- Run tabletop: simulate canary + region outage and validate fallback order (scheduled 2024-10-08).

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally pragmatic: favors clear separation of duties over theoretical purity. Looking for feedback on where orchestration responsibilities should bleed into gateway (esp. tenant isolation) and on the best format for adapter capability descriptors.

References / links
- PLAT-1243 incident writeup (linked above)
- Draft schema for adapter heartbeat: github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/blob/main/docs/adapter-heartbeat.md (WIP)
- Slack thread: #control-plane-routing (see messages ~Sep 2024)

---
Small scratch list (short):
- [ ] define capacity_hint schema (owner: Marisol)
- [ ] infra test harness for cross-region failover (owner: Daniel)
- [ ] integration test: gateway + router-proxy cache hit latency

End of doc.
